topics.label: Course introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This section introduces the lecturer, the course context, and the key learning outcomes regarding cancer causation.

topics.label: Endogenous mechanisms, genetic predisposition, and environmental epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the overarching framework of cancer causation by evaluating the relative contributions of endogenous mutations, genetic inheritance, and environmental exposures.

topics.label: Pathogen-driven carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how infectious pathogens contribute to malignant transformation, highlighting Burkitt lymphoma as a primary case study.

topics.label: Mechanisms of chemical and physical mutagens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the biochemical mechanisms through which specific dietary, radiation, and environmental mutagens induce DNA damage.

topics.label: Tumor promotion, inflammation, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how non-mutagenic promotional stimuli, inflammatory microenvironments, and proliferative host cell contexts facilitate tumor development.

topics.label: Methods for identifying and testing carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics outline the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to detect and evaluate carcinogenicity.

topics.label: Summary and risk-benefit balance
topics.groupedBecause: This concluding subtopic summarizes the main lecture themes and considers how carcinogen exposure risks are balanced against practical benefits.
